lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is Tuesday's BOCC Special Meeting, where commissioners are continuing a public hearing on adopting the 2024 International Codes and Colorado's new low-energy building standards — rules that will directly shape what gets built in this county for years to come. The BOCC will also take up 2027 nonprofit funding. Elsewhere, Town P&Z holds work sessions on a school-district employee housing proposal at the middle-high school site and another ongoing topic, while the Resident Advisory Committee digs into tenant surveys, vacancies, and housing policy.

notable.stake: Public hearing on new building codes that will define how and what gets built countywide.
Early-stage school-district employee housing project and continued zoning discussion up for review.
Town housing committee reviews tenant surveys, vacancies, and deed-restricted unit policies.
Subcommittee selects winter vendors for Gondola Plaza and appoints a new chairperson.
